articles.headline: Naomi Osaka shares vulnerable message about her 'wildest dreams' on 29th birthday
keyFacts: Tennis player Naomi Osaka shared a reflective birthday message about evaluating her life achievements as she turns 29.
Osaka stated that she is learning to recognize her accomplishments instead of feeling like she is constantly falling behind.
Osaka concluded that her current life has exceeded her childhood expectations and she wants to enjoy every moment.
body: She then shared, "somehow every year without fail I become extremely emotional around my birthday," before adding that she is reviewing her life inside her head.
“When I was younger I used to think that I was always falling behind, my yearly life reviews would make me feel like everything I had accomplished wasn’t good enough and I had to keep doing more.”
As Osaka enters her last year of her 20s, she is learning about how she evaluates herself.
“As I’m nearing the end of my 20’s I’ve started to understand that I had actually acquired the tools to escape this figurative ‘cage’ that I have felt trapped in a long time ago.”

Osaka has accomplished a lot in her career, winning four Grand Slam championships, seven career WTA singles titles, competing at the 2020 Tokyo Games, and was a part of the Opening Ceremony as she lit the Olympic cauldron, to name a few. She reflected on her "wildest dreams" later in the letter.
“Life is so full of unexpected surprises and challenges, thinking on it as a kid would I have ever guessed I would end up here? Absolutely not. Is this life beyond my wildest dreams? Absolutely.”
She concluded her letter by sharing that she wants to enjoy every second of her life, even the tough moments.

This year alone, Osaka reached the fourth round of the French Open for the first time in her career and round 16 of the US Open. The tennis star is known for her fashion statements, and during her run at the US Open she went viral for her Allen Iverson-inspired look.

articles.headline: GOP Sens. Ted Cruz, Susan Collins join growing list of targets of suspicious ‘white powder’ mailings
keyFacts: The offices of several lawmakers, including Republican Sens. Ted Cruz and Susan Collins, received suspicious envelopes containing an unknown white powder.
The FBI, Capitol Police, and Postal Inspection Service are investigating suspicious mailings sent to over a dozen congressional and state election offices.
The FBI described the powder as an unknown substance after Capitol Police issued a warning and photo of the envelopes to Senate offices.
body: The offices of Republican Sens. Ted Cruz and Susan Collins received envelopes Friday containing a “white powder,” putting the number of lawmakers targeted by the suspicious mailings at more than dozen.
The FBI, US Postal Inspection Service and Capitol Police are investigating the letters, some of which have been intercepted before reaching their destination.

“This afternoon, my Houston office received a suspicious piece of mail containing a white powder substance,” Cruz (R-Texas) wrote on X. “The FBI, Houston Police and Fire Department, and U.S. Capitol Police responded swiftly.”
Cruz called the incident “deeply concerning,” and added that the “attempts to intimidate your political opponents have no place in our country.”

A similar letter addressed to Collins (R-Maine) arrived at her Portland office, prompting an evacuation and emergency response. A separate letter was also mailed to Collins’ Washington, DC, office but was intercepted by US Capitol Police.

“Thank you to the Portland police, the Portland fire department, the hazmat team, and the FBI their quick and courageous response,” Katie Brown, the senator’s chief of staff, said in a statement to local outlets. “This was the fourth attack targeting Sen Collins’ office or home in the past two months.
“Despite escalating political rhetoric and harassment, we will continue our work for the people of Maine.”
Cruz and Collins are both locked in close midterm reelection battles.
Senate offices received a warning about the letters on Thursday from Capitol Police, which included an image of what the suspicious envelopes looked like.
Sen. Mike Rounds (R-S.D.) said his staffers did not open a “suspicious piece of mail” that arrived at his office in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, on Friday because of the law enforcement warning.

“I am grateful for the U.S. Capitol Police, who intercepted other letters and sent out a warning allowing my team to recognize this letter before opening it, and to the Sioux Falls Police Department,” Rounds wrote on X. “I am also grateful for all of my team members, who work tirelessly on behalf of South Dakotans despite the risks involved.”
The senator added, “This situation is deeply concerning and follows a trend of intimidating tactics that impact our team members. This has no place in our nation. America is better than this.”

The Senate warning included a photo of one of the suspicious envelopes that was postmarked “DSA” and gave a return address at the same Financial District building — 75 Maiden Lane — that the Democratic Socialists of America formerly listed on their membership forms.
“DSA has not occupied this office address since 2013,” a rep for the organization said in a statement. “We are also no longer headquartered at 75 Maiden Lane.”
Apart from the three GOP Senate offices that received letters Friday, at least 15 offices of congressional Democrats and some 26 state election offices have also been targeted, according to NBC News.
New York Reps. Laura Gillen, Tom Suozzi and Ritchie Torres, and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) are among the Democratic lawmakers that have confirmed having received letters.
The FBI has not said what the white powder inside the envelopes is, only describing it as “an unknown substance.”
Congressional offices have been targeted in the past with contaminated letters, most notably in a series of anthrax attacks in 2001 that sent the deadly bacteria to Senate offices.
One of those letters arrived at then-Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle’s (D-SD) office in October of that year, forcing staff to seek treatment while an entire building was later decontaminated.
The mailing spree killed five people and sickened at least 17.
Letters containing ricin, a poison, have also been mailed to Senate offices in the past, but didn’t result in any deaths.

articles.headline: Southern California wildfire engulfs homes, prompts evacuation orders
keyFacts: The Norte Fire in Southern California damaged or destroyed at least six homes and scorched up to 570 acres, fire officials said.
Officials placed approximately 16,000 residents across 6,000 homes under evacuation orders as the fire spread between San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano.
High heat and low humidity conditions contributing to fire growth are expected to last through Saturday night, according to forecasters.
body: A fast-spreading wildfire in Orange County, in Southern California, has engulfed several coastal properties and prompted widespread evacuation orders.

The Orange County Fire Authority said on Friday that the Norte Fire had scorched about 188 hectares (465 acres), with the state’s Cal Fire agency putting it at about 231 hectares (570 acres) by the evening, and that at least six homes had been damaged or destroyed in the San Juan Capistrano area.
The fire authority said firefighters were “aggressively attacking the fire from the ground and air” and issued pleas for people to stay clear of the area.
Unseasonably high temperatures and low humidity are fuelling the rapid growth of the fire, the AFP news agency reported.

The Norte Fire started in the coastal city of San Clemente on Friday and moved to the city of San Juan Capistrano, with some 6,000 homes and 16,000 residents under evacuation orders by the evening. An evacuation shelter has opened in each city while helicopters attempt to douse the flames.
Intense warm winds
The Norte Fire is one of several in the region driven by Santa Ana winds, intense warm gusts that blow from the southwest US interior towards the California coast.
The Santa Ana winds typically arrive in the autumn, right when Southern California’s vegetation is at its driest after a long, rainless summer, according to The Weather Channel.
Forecasters said winds blew at between 55km/h and 90km/h (35mph and 55mph) within coastal areas.
The strongest winds were expected through Friday, but the high heat and low humidity conditions that contribute to the growth of the fire are expected to last through Saturday night.
Tens of thousands of people in Los Angeles County were left without power as authorities attempted to lessen the possibility of electrical sparks that the heavy wind gusts could carry.
Other ongoing fires

California firefighters were also busy battling the Bryson Fire, which broke out on the outskirts of the Malibu beach community in Los Angeles County on Thursday. As of Friday, the fire had burned about 59 hectares (147 acres) and was 17 percent contained, according to Cal Fire.

The Henderson Fire was 20 percent contained and had burned 842 hectares (2,080 acres) in San Diego County by Friday, Cal Fire said. The blaze impacted Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton and prompted freeway closures.

articles.headline: Three men jailed for 158 years each for murdering Australian and US surfers in Mexico
keyFacts: A Mexican judge sentenced three men to 158 years and nine months in prison each for murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and US friend Carter Rhoad.
The court heard during the trial that the three surfers were killed in 2024 during an apparent botched truck robbery on a secluded beach in Baja California.
The victims' bodies were discovered down a well with gunshot wounds to their heads after the killings shocked communities in Mexico and Australia.
body: - Published
A Mexican judge has sentenced three men convicted of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, and their US friend Carter Rhoad to 158 years and nine months in jail each.
The Robinsons and Rhoad were killed in an apparent botched robbery of their truck on a secluded beach in Baja California in 2024 while they were on a surfing trip, the court heard during the trial.
The murders sent shockwaves around the world, particularly in Australia, as the area is usually safe from the violence seen in other parts of Mexico.
The guilty verdict was handed down last week. Debra Robinson, the brothers' mother, told the courtroom that her sons' murders had taken "the future we had imagined with them".
The convicted killers' full names could not be given for legal reasons, and they were only identified as JesÃºs Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Ãngel JesÃºs.

In November last year, the girlfriend of the alleged ringleader, JesÃºs Gerardo (alias "El Kekas"), was sentenced in a separate trial to 20 years in prison. She had admitted to involvement in the robbery.
The court heard that the bodies of the victims were found dumped down a well with gunshot wounds to their heads.
At the time, the murders shocked locals and tourists in the beach town of Ensenada who were disturbed at the apparent ease and sheer pointlessness of the killings.
Ensenada has a reputation as a welcoming spot for surfers, but the chilling murders revealed how commonplace such extreme violence remains in Mexico.
The only explanation the authorities were able to give was that the surfers - all in their early 30s - had ultimately been murdered for being in the wrong place at the wrong time.
Their killings happened barely 36 hours after they crossed into Mexico from the US. Their bodies, however, were not found for another week, when their families were able to identify them.

Local surfers also called for greater security for residents and visiting tourists, citing other recent examples of violence in the state. Tourism is a key part of the regional economy in Baja California.

articles.headline: Trump waives Russia sanctions ordered by law named for Lindsey Graham
keyFacts: President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday indefinitely waiving sweeping Russian sanctions and tariffs from a bill championed by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham.
Trump stated in a written certification to Congress that suspending the legislation is in the national interests of the United States.
Sen. Elizabeth Warren criticized the decision, stating that waiving the sanctions enables Russian President Vladimir Putin to continue his war of aggression.
body: President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday that waived the sweeping Russian sanctions and tariffs enacted by the bill championed by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham .

Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act into law last month, but he decided to put the legislation on hold indefinitely, saying that doing so is in the “national interests” of the United States.

“Section 115 of the Graham Act authorizes the President to waive the application of any sanctions provision with respect to a foreign person, any restriction with respect to a person, and any duty under the Graham Act, subject to the submission to the Congress of a written certification that such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States and a report explaining the basis for the certification,” Trump wrote in the late-night executive order .
The president confirmed he submitted a written certification to Congress explaining his decision.
Trump has been softening his stance on Russia in recent days.

The waiver comes one week after he announced the U.S. made a deal to purchase Russian diesel in an attempt to bring down global energy prices before the midterm elections . The agreement has drawn bipartisan backlash, as lawmakers worry it’s a sign that the U.S. is undermining Ukraine in its war with Russia.
This is one reason for the renewed tensions that flared between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in the past week.

The two world leaders are at odds over whether Ukraine should strike Russian oil refineries in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Zelensky gave the order to resume Ukrainian strikes this week, effectively ending a Trump-brokered energy ceasefire that Russia did not honor.

Before announcing the supposed energy-related truce, Trump called on Zelensky to step down and let a newly elected leader take his place. In response, Zelensky said he would organize a presidential election in Ukraine if Russia agrees to a two-month ceasefire. Russia rejected the proposal.

There has also been a dispute over the U.S. allegedly limiting Ukraine’s access to Starshield, a military-grade satellite network created by SpaceXAI and owned by the Department of War . The satellite system slowed down, affecting Ukraine’s ability to use Starshield for battlefield communications and operations.
Regarding the waived bill, the sanctions and tariffs that would have imposed economic leverage on Russia to end its war with Ukraine are no longer taking effect.

Under the measure, Trump had 30 days to impose 100% tariffs on goods from the top five nations that purchase Russian crude oil, place 500% tariffs on U.S. imports of Russian goods, and slap a number of Russian entities with sanctions. The one-month deadline, which started when Trump signed the legislation on Sept. 18, would have expired on Sunday.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), who voted against Graham’s bill in August, sharply criticized the president for waiving it.

“For the past 20 months, Donald Trump has failed to use his broad, existing sanctions authority to disrupt support for Russia’s war machine and to help achieve a just peace for Ukraine,” Warren said in a satement. “Tonight’s announcement is another abject and predictable failure in leadership. By waiving these sanctions, Trump is thumbing his nose at Congress’s direction that he ratchet up pressure on the Kremlin and enabling Vladimir Putin to continue his war of aggression.”

articles.headline: This easy Garmin quiz will find your perfect smartwatch
keyFacts: TechRadar released a personality quiz designed to help users select a Garmin smartwatch model.
The five-question quiz determines a recommended watch based on exercise preferences, budget, and size.
The quiz creator stated that the tool is based on years of testing and reviewing Garmin devices.
body: Which Garmin watch is right for you? If you don't know which of the best Garmin watches to choose from, shopping for smartwatches can be a very frustrating experience.

Browsing the website, you have to deal with weird names like 'Fenix' and 'Vivoactive' and many of the watches offer the same features, making the brand's offerings tough to separate. What are the differences, for example, between a Forerunner 70, 170, 570 and 970? Should you get an Instinct 3, or a Venu 4?

That's where I come in. I've been writing about Garmins for many years. I've reviewed or tested almost every modern Garmin watch, and I've taken my knowledge and condensed it into one handy flowchart personality quiz.

All you need to do is click on the quiz below and answer five easy questions, only the first of which is multiple choice, to get my recommendation for your ideal smartwatch. I've even linked the full review of each watch, so you can read more about it and find the best deals.
The quiz operates first by finding out your preferred forms of exercise, then hits criteria like budget, watch size, importance of outdoor features, and so on.

articles.headline: Trump puts new Russia sanctions passed by Congress on hold amid deepening row with Ukraine
keyFacts: President Donald Trump issued an executive order waiving new bipartisan congressional sanctions against the Russian economy.
The paused legislation targets Russian banks, officials, and energy shipping to restrict financial resources fueling Russia's war in Ukraine.
Trump said Russia will supply an additional 500,000 metric tons of diesel in November under their purchase agreement.
body: Donald Trump has put on hold a sweeping new sanctions package targeting the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause on the legislation passed by both chambers was in the national interest.

In an executive order on Friday, the US president said he was waiving many sanctions, restrictions and duties on Russia, in a move that comes as he has been publicly criticising Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, including suggesting that Ukraine needs a new leader.

Trump signed the legislation last month, after Congress passed the measure in an act of rare bipartisan agreement. It sought to clamp down more quickly on the flow of financial resources fuelling Russia’s war against Ukraine.

The legislation – whose primary backer in Congress was the late senator Lindsey Graham – sanctions Russian officials, banks and a shadow fleet of tankers that keeps Russian energy moving and was due to be implemented in two days.

It also directs Trump to impose up to 100% tariffs on the top five importers of Russian oil or natural gas, with an exception for countries that import less than 15% of Russia’s natural gas exports and have taken significant steps to reduce those imports.

Friday’s announcement comes a week after Trump said the US had agreed to purchase diesel from Russia to try to bring down global energy prices, upending years of US and western pressure on the Kremlin to end its war against Ukraine.

Trump said last week that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1m tons “immediately thereafter”. Russia would deliver an additional 3m tons “within a short period of time” after that, he wrote.
The president has face widespread criticism after making the announcement, with a dozen US senators – including six Republicans – calling on Trump to rescind his diesel deal.

A letter from the bipartisan group of lawmakers sent on Tuesday urged Trump to execute the sanctions authorities included in the legislation passed last month, called the “Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026”.

Under the legislation he signed into law, Trump had until 18 October to impose the sanctions and tariffs on Russian energy, or waive them. The administration had not told lawmakers whether it would impose the sanctions or issue a waiver.
Zelenskyy said on Friday the diesel deal would mean cash “will start flowing back into Russia”, as he met European leaders in Brussels.

Trump blindsided Zelenskyy last weekend by announcing that Ukraine and Russia had agreed not to target each other’s energy facilities. Facing midterm elections next month, Trump has blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for pushing up energy prices that could cost his Republican party its thin majorities in the US Senate and House of Representatives.

Trump’s administration is suspected of withholding intelligence from Ukraine on incoming Russian ballistic missile strikes, and of throttling Starshield, the military version of the Starlink satellite internet network, to prevent it from being used on drones flying faster than 100mph (161km/h). Neither has officially been confirmed.

The US sanctions legislation has also become a campaign centerpiece for Senator Darline Graham, Lindsey Graham’s sister appointed to serve out the remaining months of his term, who is also running to replace him in the Senate more permanently.

In a debate earlier this week with South Carolina Democratic nominee Annie Andrews, Graham – who has Trump’s endorsement and is expected to campaign with him in South Carolina next week – said she had been “so proud” to help get the measure passed but acknowledged it was Trump’s purview as to how he implemented it.

“It gives the president tools that he can use, if he so chooses, to end the war through economic sanctions,” Graham during the debate in Columbia. “So that’s up to him as to whether or not he wants to use it, or whether he wants to use something else, but I think the purpose of it is to bring down the gas prices and ultimately end the war. And when the war ends, gas prices will fall.”
With Reuters and the Associated Press

articles.headline: Mark Wahlberg wants to take on the longevity-startup crowd with an affordable gym concept
keyFacts: Actor Mark Wahlberg announced that his first Municipal Gym will open outside Las Vegas in December.
Wahlberg said the 32,000-square-foot club will offer blood work and wellness services at an affordable price point compared to luxury longevity clubs.
Wahlberg stated he plans an aggressive growth strategy for the gyms to build a comprehensive health and wellness ecosystem.
body: Mark Wahlberg has started companies of his own and backed plenty of others. But the gym he’s opening in December, he says, has him more excited than anything he’s done in his entire career. It also goes after a corner of the market where venture money keeps flowing: pricey, diagnostics-heavy wellness.

Speaking with us at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco on Thursday, the actor said the first Municipal Gym opens in December. It’s a 32,000-square-foot club outside Las Vegas with blood work, epigenetic testing, recovery gear, compression therapy, cold plunges, and a café that serves up protein muffins, among other things. He’s pitching it as the affordable alternative to the longevity clubs that charge tens of thousands of dollars a year for much the same thing.
It’s the second part of a scheme that was, in some ways, first hatched seven years ago, with a casual sportswear line.

The clothing brand Municipal launched during COVID, which Wahlberg volunteers “was not a good idea.” (Clothing was a lousy business to enter in 2020, with retailers from J.Crew to Brooks Brothers going bankrupt.)

It grew out of what he’d been seeing as a celebrity fitness spokesperson. He’d done collabs with various brands, and other companies kept approaching him to be their brand ambassador, but they all seemed to want the same thing, he said. “Everybody just kind of wanted to sell T-shirts and sneakers. And I was like, well, I want to kind of have a bigger impact on people’s lives as a whole.”

By that, he meant what people eat, what supplements they take, how they train, and how they recover. Clothing was just the start. “We figured, okay, we’ll start in the apparel space, and then we’ll build from there.” He says he only takes swings at “things that I’m very passionate about and things that are a direct extension of who I am.”

Even without a pandemic, clothing is a brutal business, as we pointed out, citing Lululemon’s repeated quality-control challenges. But Wahlberg didn’t seem fazed, talking instead about why the gym fits his vision. He thought it “always could be great for the brand” in part because it gives people a place to “actually feel and touch the clothes” before they buy. Besides, he continued, how people exercise is “another big part of people’s lives.”

Most in the space have been laser-focused on the high end. Fountain Life, the longevity company co-founded by Tony Robbins, raised $18 million last year to expand its centers for wealthy clients, and a full subscription runs $21,500 a year, according to reports. The Estate, a company co-founded by Robbins and hospitality executive Sam Nazarian, is still mapping out plans to charge $35,000 memberships to its wellness centers. Equinox is similarly taking names for a $36,000 longevity add-on that it plans to launch atop a traditional gym membership.

Wahlberg says Municipal aims for that same luxury tier but for a lot less. “We have a better price point than our competitors, and we’re going to get far more results,” he said. For $99, he said as an example, members will receive three rounds of blood work and an hour with a doctor to flag what they’re predisposed to. Supplements and hormone therapy are also “right there.”

When we asked whether the gyms double as storefronts for his other products (he owns a supplements brand), he said “kind of.” What he’s really building, he said, is a “health and wellness ecosystem” with “everything there, soup to nuts.”

He didn’t put a number on how many gyms he wants, but he called the growth strategy “aggressive,” telling us that “landlords and developers who toured the Las Vegas site have offered “AAA locations at very favorable terms, with great TI” (tenant-improvement allowances that help pay for the build-out).

Wahlberg’s record in fitness might scare off someone else. We told him we’d recently watched “Wahl Street,” his reality show, in which an early episode shows him getting deeply involved with the fitness chain F45 in 2019, and that we wanted to warn him about what was coming. “How did you know about the pandemic?” he joked, to laughs from the crowd. He bought into the company, known for its 45-minute classes, at a $450 million valuation. It went public in 2021, then was delisted from the NYSE in 2023 after its stock collapsed. Wahlberg said he learned a lot from the experience.

“I think the biggest takeaway was just making sure that I’m involved with people that share the same approach that I do.” He also said he always thought big box was the better model. F45’s classes suit people who are short on time, but he wants members to hang around Municipal for hours. Plenty of gyms run on a “join up but don’t show up” model, he said, adding: “I can’t understand that philosophy.”

The name Municipal is very intentional and clearly means a lot to Wahlberg, who grew up poor in Boston, one of nine kids, playing on public basketball courts and golf courses. “You learn a lot on the blacktop,” he said. “You learn to win, to lose, to compete, and hopefully to get back up and do it again.”
He has never hidden his rough youth. (He was sentenced to two years for assaults as a teenager and served 45 days.)

In fact, earlier in the afternoon on Thursday, surrounded by friends and business associates in a seating area backstage — this is the man who inspired the show “Entourage” after all — he said he was turned around by two people, including Father Jim Flavin, a Boston-area parish priest who has been in Wahlberg’s life since he was 13.

He wants the gyms to carry that same spirit. “It’s a place to work, but have fun and support each other and create community and really challenge people to be better versions of themselves,” he said. It’s personal, he said outright. “I’ve come from next to nothing to being in an amazing position,” Wahlberg said. “I try to constantly remind myself that I can inspire other people growing up in similar situations, especially inner-city kids and at-risk youth, that there is a way to overcome your circumstances if you’re willing to go out there and do the work.”

At 55, he added, his goals have changed; while he was once focused on looking good, “I just want to feel good when I wake up in the morning,” he said. “I want to be able to conquer all the things that I have planned for the day.”

He also said his plate is exceedingly full right now, between the gym, a film role as Pete Rose, and his daughter’s equestrian career. He’s so eager for the gym to open, he said, that visiting the construction site feels like “literally watching paint dry.” Indeed, asked if he was open to taking on new ventures, he shrugged. “I’m not out there hunting, looking for the next thing for sure.” But he wouldn’t rule it out, he added quickly. “If something amazing were to come along, obviously I wouldn’t turn it down.”

body: US sanctions on Russia will not take effect as planned after President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday waiving them for national security reasons.
"As described further in section 4 of this order, I am hereby waiving the application of such sanctions, restrictions, and duties provided for in the Graham Act," the executive order said.

"I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver at this time is in the national interests of the United States," Trump said in the order released by the White House.
The White House did not immediately explain how Trump's decision to pause the sanctions will serve the national interest.
The White House posted the decision on its website late in the evening. It noted that the report explaining the decision had been submitted to Congress.
According to the order, the waiver will remain in effect until Trump or his top officials determine that "further action is appropriate."
Trump's controversial deal with Russia
The Lindsey Graham Act, which was named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill, had found bipartisan support in Congress and was passed in September.
It allowed the Trump administration to increase pressure on Russia over its war against Ukraine by imposing duties up to 100& on major buyers of Russian oil.

The sanctions were meant to starve Russian President Vladimir Putin of the resources needed to continue its war in Ukraine. The bill aimed to penalize Russian officials, banks and a shadow fleet of tankers that keeps Russian energy moving.
India, one of the biggest buyers of Russian oil, was among the countries that raised concerns about the Russia sanctions.

Now, the move to waive the sanctions against Russia comes a week after Trump said the US had agreed to purchase diesel from Russia to try and bring down global energy prices, despite that potentially hurting Ukraine in its war with Russia.

With US midterms just around the corner, the sanctions on Russia could have risked raising oil prices even further while Americans are already grappling with increased costs largely because of the US-Israeli war on Iran, analysts have said.

Senator Richard Blumenthal, a Democrat who also drafted the bill with sanctions against Russia, said Trump was turning his back on "the majority of Americans, their representatives in both houses of Congress, and our European allies."
"These waivers have nothing to do with our national security, and everything to do with sucking up to Vladimir Putin," Blumenthal said.

articles.headline: The Tesla Roadster should go into production in 2028, but don't get your hopes up
keyFacts: Tesla announced that its redesigned Roadster sports car is targeting a 2028 production window with a price of $250,000 for the reserve trim.
CEO Elon Musk stated during an October event that the company will enter production in 2028.
The Roadster was originally unveiled in November 2017 with a targeted 2020 release, but it has faced multiple years of delays.
body: The Tesla Roadster should go into production in 2028, but don't get your hopes up
I drive upside down on the boulevard of broken dreams.

Tesla dominated the headlines on Thursday thanks to a very cool stunt. In announcing the redesigned Roadster at its October 15 event, the electric car company put some jet fuel in the mix. After driving up a C-shaped ramp on a suction rig until it was upside-down, the Roadster floated to the ground on rocket boosters. We also learned that the new sports car is targeting a 2028 production window and that it will cost $250,000 to reserve the "Thrust" trim level with cold-gas thrusters. "We enter production in 2028," Musk said during the event. "Actually, for real."

If you're feeling a bit of deja vu, don't worry — you're firmly within your faculties. This is not the first time Tesla has announced the second-generation Roadster, and the company hasn't exactly drawn attention to that fact with this re-announced version. Still, the question on many minds is whether this is another paper launch for Tesla's embattled second-gen sports car.

The first Roadster was a milestone for Tesla in its early days. Released in 2008 and produced in very limited numbers, the car was ideated by one of Tesla's original founders, Martin Eberhard, before current CEO Elon Musk had bought Eberhard and his partner, Marc Tarpenning, out of the company. It was the idea of the Roadster which initially drew Musk to the fledgling startup in 2004 and prompted his initial investment in the company. He would go on to oversee the production of that sports car. Crammed inside the chassis of a Lotus Elise, it was truly impressive at the time to see a battery-powered vehicle able to reach 244 miles on a charge.

The redesigned Roadster was first unveiled in November 2017, promising to be the apex of Tesla's innovations in electric vehicle manufacturing. Musk called it "a hardcore smackdown to gasoline cars." Targeted for a 2020 release, it was shown off alongside the Tesla Semi, a Class 8 electric semitruck which also stalled in production. In Feburary 2018, Musk promised a "SpaceX" package that would "include ~10 small rocket thrusters arranged seamlessly around the car" and would "dramatically improve acceleration, top speed, braking and cornering."

Then the delays began. With Tesla still accepting deposits starting at $50,000 and extending up to $250,000, the initial 2020 production window came and went. In a July 2020 earnings call for Tesla, Musk said production would begin within the following year to 18 months. With the globe engulfed in a public health crisis, the delay wasn't the most shocking of developments. Ironically, Musk noted in an interview with Joe Rogan that same year that he wanted to build the Cybertruck first — a mission accomplished after years of that vehicle's own delays.

But a year and a half after the initial delay, there was no Roadster in sight. Musk delayed the car to 2022 in early 2021, but by the end of the year, that projection had slipped to 2023. The CEO announced further delays in 2023 and 2024.

And those years have been bizarre for Musk and Tesla, to say the least. The CEO has undergone a public transformation from public environmentalist to far-right political kingmaker, a period which culminated in a slash-and-burn of the Federal government as he headed up president Donald Trump's newly formed Department of Government Efficiency. By July 2025, The Lancet had published a study projecting the cuts could lead to more than 14 million deaths by 2030. Musk has disputed those numbers, but the reputational damage his stint in government caused spilled over to Tesla, leading to widespread global protests against the company. As Musk stepped down from DOGE in May 2025, dogged by allegations of substance abuse and family drama, the Roadster may not have been near the top of the billionaire's priority list.

By the time Tesla recommitted to releasing the Roadster this past April, many had given up hope that the sports car would ever make it to market. Tesla's failure to deliver the vehicle had long ago become pop-cultural joke fodder, and even Tesla owners such as YouTuber Marques Brownlee, who had interviewed Musk multiple times on his MKBHD channel, fretted on his Waveform podcast in September 2025, "Tesla has been sitting with my 50 grand for eight years and hasn't done anything with it." Another high-profile figure to complain about their Roadster reservations included Musk's erstwhile business partner and current rival Sam Altman of OpenAI.

It's worth noting that a launch event without a firm launch date isn't much of a launch. Even after Tesla's impressive October event, Musk and company will need to convince potential customers that putting down a deposit for the Roadster is a better investment than burning a pile of money with a Boring Company flamethrower.

articles.headline: Kamario Taylor injury presents LSU, Lane Kiffin a layup they can't afford to miss in CFP chase
keyFacts: Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor and top rusher Fluff Bothwell are listed as doubtful for Saturday's game against LSU due to injuries.
LSU enters the matchup as a 17-point favorite as the Tigers attempt to revive their College Football Playoff hopes.
Mississippi State may turn to Parker Billy Puckett or AJ Swann to replace Taylor at quarterback.
body: If LSU is going to squirm its way back into the College Football Playoff conversation following a 4-2 start and salvage an uninspired start to Lane Kiffin's coaching tenure, it's going to need good fortune and better football.

Whether the No. 22 Tigers will play good football when they host No. 16 Mississippi State on Saturday is to be determined, but LSU is undoubtedly beginning the second half of its season with some good fortune. With Bulldogs star quarterback Kamario Taylor and top rusher Fluff Bothwell both listed as doubtful on Friday night's SEC student-athlete availability report, the Tigers appear to have been handed a layup.

Taking advantage of it will be critical for a Tigers team that still plays No. 6 Alabama, No. 7 Texas and No. 14 Tennessee. After opening as a 10.5-point favorite amid uncertainty over Taylor's status, the Tigers are now favored by 17. With Mississippi State's breakout star likely to be sidelined by a foot injury that he suffered in a Week 5 loss to Alabama, the Bulldogs have lost their bite.

The expected absence of Bothwell will only make life harder on Mississippi State's offense as it potentially navigates life without Taylor, who ranks No. 5 nationally in total offense per game at 321.8 yards.
Turning the page for LSU

Mississippi State's hobbled status gives the Tigers a great chance to start anew in the second half of the season after road losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky sullied the beginning of Kiffin's highly anticipated first season. While conventional wisdom suggests the Tigers need to win out and finish 10-2 to reach the CFP, there may still be some wiggle room.

If the Tigers finish 9-3, they will have an 84.9% chance of reaching the CFP, according to the CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster. In that scenario, they would need to go 5-1 overall and 3-1 against the four teams remaining on their schedule who are currently ranked in the top 20 of the AP poll. Three of those four top-20 games are at home, including Saturday's tilt against Mississippi State.
Such an outcome is squarely within the realm of possibility for an LSU team that flashed its high-end potential in dominant victories over the likes of Clemson and Texas A&M.

Getting to 9-3 or 10-2 will require cleaner play on both sides of the football for LSU. Turnovers have been a recurring issue for the Tigers, who are tied for 117th with 10 giveaways. The defense has been inconsistent, allowing fewer than 200 yards in each of LSU's four wins and 400+ yards in the two losses.

But the idea of the Tigers figuring things out in the season's second half isn't outlandish. Flashes of potency have been there, even during its losses. LSU averaged 5.8 yards per play against Kentucky and racked up 26 first downs. The Tigers also scored 17 unanswered on Ole Miss in the second half before faltering late.
Where Mississippi State will turn

After Taylor, Mississippi State's second quarterback is listed as redshirt freshman Parker "Billy" Puckett" or fifth-year player AJ Swann. Puckett, a formerly unranked in-state prospect, has handled second-team snaps for the Bulldogs so far this season, completing 8 of 14 passes for 89 yards.

Swann is a former Vanderbilt starter who spent the 2024 season at LSU before transferring to Appalachian State last year. Now on his fourth school in five years — and third SEC program — he brings some experience to the position.

But there's no replacing Taylor, who carried the Bulldogs to a 4-0 start before Mississippi State took a 56-23 loss against Alabama. He appeared to suffer the foot injury late in that defeat. Even after a bye week, it remains an issue.
Former Georgia, Arizona State and Sacramento State quarterback Jaden Rashada is also on the Mississippi State roster, though he was not listed on this week's depth chart.

articles.headline: Tech founder criticized for vibe coding game about shooting 'zombies' in San Francisco's poorest neighborhood

body: Pierre-Louis Biojout, founder of Y Combinator-backed AI startup NanoCorp, took heat from San Francisco residents and city leaders this week after publishing a weekend vibe coding project: a web-based shooter set in SF's Tenderloin district, which is known for homelessness and open drug use.

"San Francisco couldn't fix the Tenderloin," Biojout said in a now-deleted X post on October 13. "So I monetized it [as a] Call of Duty style zombie shooter on the real SF streets." He noted that he'd already made $300 from in-game ads.
The game, called Tenderloin Night Shift, had players shoot "zombies" that, according to reports from the SF Chronicle and KRON4 news, included a "folded" fentanyl addict and a Black security guard.

Speaking to the Chronicle, Jennifer Friedenbach, executive director of the SF Coalition on Homelessness, said that Biojout was "monetizing the dehumanization and pretend killing for fun of mostly Black and Brown residents of the poorest neighborhood in San Francisco."
In a correspondence with the paper, Biojout said that he had not intended to "provoke or to depict shooting real people" and that the game also included tech workers as characters.
Tenderloin Night Shift appears to have been removed from NanoCorp's website. Although Biojout deleted his X post, the discourse that ensued remains.
"You made a game about shooting people in active addiction," said another tech founder. "These are human beings, not zombies. show me the positive side of this - i'm probably blind."

"Why are you talking about addiction? It's a zombie shooter," Biojout said in response.

Some commenters, however, expressed approval for the message Biojout has disavowed. "They are currently NOT human beings," said one user, while another said they'd "train in bro's game" to prepare to visit San Francisco.

Tyler grew up in Silicon Valley during the '80s and '90s, playing games like Zork and Arkanoid on early PCs. He was later captivated by Myst, SimCity, Civilization, Command & Conquer, all the shooters they call "boomer shooters" now, and PS1 classic Bushido Blade (that's right: he had Bleem!). articles.headline: All the news about the iPhone Duo
keyFacts: Apple announced its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, featuring a 5.4-inch outer screen and a 7.6-inch inner screen.
The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 and is scheduled to launch in stores on October 23rd.
Apple stated that preorder demand for the new foldable device was extraordinary, causing online delivery estimates to slip into next year.
body: Apple has finally announced its long-rumored foldable: the iPhone Duo.

The new phone has a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display, a “nano‑texture” finish on the inner screen, and barely any visible crease. Instead of Face ID, it uses Touch ID on the power button. It has two cameras, a main lens and a wide-angle lens. Apple completely revamped iOS 27’s controls and apps for the foldable, including putting the dock on the side of the phone. And it has a flashy opening animation when you unfold the phone.

The iPhone Duo a big new bet from Apple, though one that’s a little late to the game compared to competitors like Samsung and Google. The phone isn’t cheap: it starts at $1,999 for the base 256GB model, and the prices only go up from there. Still, Apple said that preorder demand was “extraordinary,” so it could have a hit on its hands.
Here’s everything unfolding about the iPhone Duo.

- Pinned The first foldable iPhone is finally here, and following its announcement, we got the chance to try the phone for ourselves. We’ve long been told that Apple would make a foldable iPhone once the tech was good enough — has it been worth the wait? It definitely feels like something different. The inner screen has a decidedly matte finish that handled even some glare from the windows above the hands-on area well. The folding mechanism is smooth, and even IP68 rated, and the crease is almost impossible to find with my finger. The 5.4-inch outer screen looks petite by modern slab phone standards. Read Article >

- Apple says iPhone Duo preorder demand has been “extraordinary.” “The pre-order demand for iPhone Duo, our first foldable iPhone, has been nothing short of extraordinary. We are working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers’ hands as quickly as possible, and we will continue accepting orders online,” the company said in a statement. “Our teams look forward to welcoming customers at Apple Stores worldwide to experience the iPhone Duo and the incredible full iPhone line-up for themselves,” it added, without disclosing whether inventory would be available for customers who were unable to secure pre-orders when the device goes on sale Oct. 23.

- Delivery estimates for the iPhone Duo slipped into next year in less than an hour after Apple opened preorders for it at 8AM ET on Friday. At the time of writing we are seeing late January delivery dates for every configuration on Apple’s website. The foldable is slated to launch in stores on October 23rd, and Apple typically reserves some units for in-store availability. So while online orders are delayed, you might be able to get one sooner in-person at an Apple Store. Read Article >

- Few phones have been more anticipated than a foldable iPhone, but it’s finally here. The iPhone Duo was unveiled during Apple’s “Surprise and shine” event alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 models. Apple’s first foldable has a 5.4-inch outer screen, and it unfolds to show off its 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR screen. Apple Pencil support is coming later this year. While it lacks Face ID for facial unlocking, there’s a Touch ID sensor along its edge to identify your fingerprint. The device has an IP68 rating, with Ceramic Shield 2 on its back, with Ceramic Shield covering the front display. It has the same A20 Pro chipset as the iPhone 18 Pro. Notably, the Duo has the same 48-megapixel fusion camera as the 18 Pro, though it doesn’t have variable aperture. Read Article >

- Apple’s iPhone Duo foldable phone opens for preorder tomorrow, October 16th, at 8am ET / 5am PT, but you don’t have to wait until then to get your order mostly sorted. The company’s product page for the phone now lets you select the color you want, along with storage capacity, carrier preference, and whether you want to set up a trade to make the $1,999 foldable a little cheaper. Once you enter all of the details, all you’ll need to do tomorrow morning, once preorders open, is to confirm your order. It’ll be sitting in your cart ready for checkout. This will save you some time, and you’ll jump ahead of people who are still customizing their iPhone Duo details. Read Article >

- If you don’t get AppleCare Plus for the iPhone Duo, any repairs are going to be pretty expensive. Apple published the estimated repair costs for the iPhone Duo without AppleCare Plus today, as reported by MacRumors, and they can be high: Battery service, for example, will cost $229, inner display damage will cost $999, and “other damage” costs $1,499. Here’s Apple’s estimated costs for various repairs if you don’t have AppleCare Plus: Read Article >

- I’ve spent most of the last couple weeks using an otherwise unexceptional midrange Android phone with one amazing feature: a matte OLED display. That screen is by far the best thing about the TCL P80 Ultra, and weirdly, it’s made me more excited for the iPhone Duo and its matte inner display. 2023’s TCL Nxtpaper 40 first brought matte displays to the company’s phones after they appeared on tablets in 2021. Nxtpaper is more than a simple matte finish on a panel; it also includes a paperlike feel and low-power, monochrome modes that create a reasonable facsimile of an E Ink screen. But the matte effect has always been the biggest draw for me. Read Article >

- You only get one chance at a first impression, and getting to introduce Apple’s first folding phone is certainly a strong way to start things off as Apple’s CEO. On The Vergecast today, we’re talking all about Apple’s launch event: how John Ternus did in his first appearance as CEO, what we make of the new iPhones, and whether Apple is stepping into dangerous territory with its new AI features on the Apple Watch. First up, Allison Johnson joins me to discuss the new iPhones, which she had a chance to test in Cupertino. Both of us have some questions about the new variable aperture camera on the iPhone 18 Pro — and whether the real upgrade simply lies in the wider aperture, not the ability to stop it down. Then we dig into the iPhone Duo and how Apple decided to pick and choose the best parts of Android foldables. Read Article >

- Apple was far from the first company to announce a passport-shaped folding phone this year, but that doesn’t mean it wasn’t copied. As my colleague Dom Preston already explained, it’s almost impossible to keep product development secret when Apple and its competitors all share the same global suppliers. Apple’s new CEO John Ternus and head of marketing Greg ‘Joz’ Joswiak addressed the topic during an interview with TechRadar’s Lance Ulanoff and Mark Spoonauer of Tom’s Guide. Read Article >

- With the iPhone Duo, Apple has pulled off a familiar trick. It arrives into a mature Android foldable market with a handful of hardware features we’ve mostly already seen elsewhere, but paired with a level of software polish that makes a lot of them feel new again. It’s those software flourishes that have me excited to try the iPhone Duo when it launches next month, but I’m less convinced that its hardware will be anything special. If Apple had gotten there first, the Duo’s biggest surprise would have been its squat, wide, passport-inspired shape. But its slow-moving supply chain meant that Huawei, Samsung, and Xiaomi all managed to beat Apple to market with similarly sized rivals, so the unusual design already feels fairly familiar — helped by Samsung’s aggressive efforts to market its new design. Read Article >

- Apple’s foldable phone is finally here — well, almost. The iPhone Duo, coming October 23rd, follows in the footsteps of past folding devices from Android phone makers like Samsung, OnePlus, and Google, with a $1,999 price tag that sits just above the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Galaxy Z Fold 8. While its hardware bears similarities to its competitors, the iPhone Duo is one of a few models that takes a passport-like approach. The aspect ratio is the same on the inside and outside screens, and it’s even usable with some apps while partially folded. The interior screen has a special outer layer, which along with its hinge design, makes the interior crease almost impossible to spot (something that many competitors struggle to do, though Samsung and Oppo are making fantastic progress). Read Article >

- Apple has just announced its first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo. The new phone has a 5.4-inch outer screen and a 7.6-inch inner screen, two back cameras, Touch ID for authentication, an IP68 rating, and all sorts of slick software tricks to make iOS feel more at home on the new device. Preorders start on October 16th ahead of availability on October 23rd, and it starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. It’s a huge announcement for Apple, and we have many feelings about it. Here’s our gut reactions to the phone. And let us know in the comments what you think! Read Article >

- Apple just wrapped up its first iPhone launch event with CEO John Ternus at the helm, and it did not disappoint. We got a look at Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone Duo, along with the next generation of AirPods and the Apple Watch. Here’s a roundup of all the biggest announcements from the event. Read Article >

- Obviously, part of the appeal of a foldable phone is all that additional screen real estate. That gives you plenty of room for some serious multitasking that just isn’t possible, or at the very least is clunky, on a smaller screen. Apple rarely does things without seriously considering all the implications, so it was never just going to shove iOS as-is into its new foldable. The company didn’t have to start from scratch or reinvent the wheel, however. It already had a mobile OS capable of multitasking in iPadOS, which was built on iOS to begin with. The company even said that the iPhone Duo was designed to be “as natural and intuitive as iPad.” Read Article >

- Apple has announced its long-anticipated foldable iPhone, which arrives more than seven years after the first Samsung Galaxy Fold phone hit the market. My colleague Allison Johnson has already had the chance to try out the device in person at Apple’s event, so read what she thinks of it so far. The Duo will be available to preorder on October 16th, going on sale on October 23rd, a month later than the two 18 Pro models. It starts at $1,999 — $100 more than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, but $100 less than its Z Fold 8 Ultra — for 256GB of storage, with the option to go up to 2TB total. Like the iPhone Air, it’s eSIM-only worldwide. Read Article >

articles.headline: Cookies, liquor and mocking Nazis fuel final stretch in fiery Texas House race
keyFacts: Federal election records show Texas Democratic congressional candidate Katy Padilla Stout reported over $4,300 in campaign spending on cookies, alcohol, and Mexican restaurant meals.
Republican opponent Brandon Herrera criticized the expenditures on a campaign website, while Stout stated the disbursements were for campaign and fundraising events supporting local businesses.
During a televised debate, Stout apologized after misspeaking when criticizing Herrera's online videos, leading to a heated exchange regarding Nazi imagery and offensive content.
body: A Texas Democratic congressional candidate's campaign reported more than $4,300 in spending on cookies, Mexican restaurant purchases and beer and wine earlier this year, according to federal election records, drawing renewed attention after a heated debate in which she apologized for a remark about her Republican opponent "making fun of Nazis."

Katy Padilla Stout, the Democrat nominee for Texas' 23rd Congressional District, reported expenditures totaling $4,338.14 in five transactions in March and April, according to spending details cited in an August report by RedState and records attributed to the Federal Election Commission (FEC).
The reported purchases included $675 for cookies for a campaign event, $1,289.22 at Total Wine and $2,373.92 at Las Guitarras Cocina Mexicana.
SENATE REPUBLICAN SETTLES SIX-YEAR-OLD CAMPAIGN BILL AFTER BEING CALLED OUT ON SOCIAL MEDIA
The expenditures have also become a line of attack for Republican Brandon Herrera, whose campaign website showcases the cookie purchase and accuses Stout of using donor funds to pay for the treats.

According to the spending details, the campaign reported a $675 payment dated March 30 with the stated purpose "COOKIES FOR EVENT." Herrera's website identifies the payee as Denise Gamboa Zelle and categorizes the expense as a campaign event expenditure.
Additional transactions included $1,089.08 at Total Wine on April 21 and $200.14 the following day, both described as "BEER AND WINE."
The campaign also reported payments of $2,027.52 and $346.40 to Las Guitarras Cocina Mexicana on April 27 and April 28, respectively, according to the transaction details.
In a statement to Fox News Digital, Stout said the disbursements "were for campaign and fundraising events which were attended by our supporters."
"Sugar cookies, particularly Texas-shaped ones, hold a special place in Texan culture," she said. "We bought ours at a local bakery because we believe in supporting small businesses."
SENATE HOPEFUL'S 'TREADING WATER' NARRATIVE CRUMBLES UNDER $500K CAMPAIGN PAYOUTS TO FAMILY

The filings establish that the campaign reported the expenditures but do not establish whether the purchases were improper, whether any were for personal use or how many people attended the associated events.
The spending has attracted criticism from Herrera's campaign, which maintains an opposition website, The Real Katy Stout.
Under a section labeled "Cookie gate," the site highlights the $675 expenditure and displays the reported purpose, "COOKIES FOR EVENT."
The website also criticizes Stout's positions on immigration, taxes and other issues.
DEM SENATE NOMINEE APOLOGIZES TO JEWISH VOTERS AFTER 'GENOCIDE' REMARK SPARKED BACKLASH

The spending questions come as the two candidates compete for a congressional seat representing one of the country's largest districts along the southern border. During Tuesday's televised debate in San Antonio, Stout also drew attention for an unusual exchange involving Herrera's online videos.

"He made millions of dollars after making jokes online, making fun of Nazis, making fun of all of these things that we know he does not need to be doing," Stout said in a heated moment during the debate.
Herrera responded, "And here I thought making fun of Nazis was a good thing."
Stout later apologized and clarified her criticism after closing remarks.
"I apologize, I did misspeak," she said. "He chooses to goose-step on YouTube for clickbait and money so that he can promote that type of ideology. He chooses to shame women."
The exchange was part of a debate hosted by WOAI/KABB, during which the congressional candidates also sparred over gun rights, immigration and the cost of living .
Stout told Fox News Digital "mocking Nazis is fine, and that is not what I objected to, nor is that what my opponent does."

"I object to content that trivializes veteran suicide, rape, child murder, women’s bodies and the Holocaust, the type of content he churns out," she added. "You can hear his disgusting commentary straight from his own mouth at HeReallySaidThat.com .

"Do I think he promotes Nazi imagery? Yes. In a video posted 5/24/22, he goose-steps to 'Erika,' and touts an MP-40 machine gun. In another video posted 6/23/20, he said 'for the fatherland' before firing a Nazi-made STG 44, calling it 'like a religious experience.'

"Calling it a joke doesn’t change what it is: giving a platform to Nazi symbols and weaponry for clicks and money. In my view, the 'I’m only joking' defense is a familiar tactic among neo-Nazi and antisemitic content creators. His content has attracted bipartisan condemnation, including the Republican Jewish Coalition, which called my opponent 'a goose-stepping extremist who pals around with online Nazis.'"
Stout, a former teacher and child welfare attorney, has emphasized affordability and corruption as central themes of her campaign.

Herrera, a firearms manufacturer and online personality who has adopted "Let's Go Brandon" as his campaign slogan, has campaigned on border law enforcement, tax reductions and Second Amendment protections.
The two are vying to replace former Republican Rep. Tony Gonzales , who resigned earlier this year after acknowledging an affair with a staffer.

Texas' 23rd Congressional District stretches from the San Antonio area toward El Paso and includes hundreds of miles of the U.S.-Mexico border. Early voting begins Oct. 19, with Election Day scheduled for Nov. 3.
The campaign for Brandon Herrera did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

articles.headline: Red Rising Greenlit for Movie Adaptation With Author Pierce Brown to Produce
keyFacts: Paramount Pictures greenlit a movie adaptation of the Red Rising book series by Pierce Brown.
Francis Lawrence will direct the film and produce it alongside the author, while Justin Rhodes will write the script.
The story follows a protagonist named Darrow who infiltrates a strict caste system in a galaxy spanning more than a decade.
body: The Red Rising book series by author Pierce Brown has officially been greenlit for a movie adaptation from Paramount Pictures, with Hunger Games alum Francis Lawrence to direct.

Red Rising is getting the Hollywood treatment more than a decade after it was first published in 2014. As confirmed by The Hollywood Reporter on October 16, Paramount Pictures has picked up the rights to the series, which will be brought to the screen by director Francis Lawrence.

Lawrence is known for his work on another young adult screen adaptation in the Hunger Games series, having directed every movie in the franchise sans the first one, which was directed by Gary Ross. Lawrence recently directed Stephen King adaptation The Long Walk , as well as the forthcoming Sunrise on the Reaping , the latest movie in the Hunger Games franchise.

Lawrence is also set to produce the Red Rising film alongside Cameron MacConomy for their about:blank production company, as well as Francesco Goedhuis and the author of the Red Rising saga himself, Pierce Brown.
Brown reacted to the news in a post on his Instagram account , writing, "Let fall the iron rain. Bloodydamn, I love this team."

Joining Red Rising is Justin Rhodes, who will write the movie’s script. Eagle-eyed IGN readers will recognize this name, as he is also involved in Netflix’s live-action Bioshock movie , which is reportedly still in early development. Rhodes is known for films like Terminator: Dark Fate, Traveler, and Liminal.

Red Rising is a sprawling book series that is planned to end with its seventh and final installment, which as yet has no release date. Set in a galaxy with a strict, color-coded caste system, the books follow Darrow, a Red — the lowest rank on the social totem pole. He and his fellow Reds toil tirelessly in the mines of Mars, with the hope that one day, they will be able to make the planet habitable for human life… but it turns out that this was already accomplished generations ago.

After learning of this massive betrayal, Darrow makes it his mission to infiltrate the highest social caste, the Golds, and set things right across the entire galaxy in a deadly conflict that spans more than a decade. If you're interested in getting into the books, you can check out our guide to navigating this sprawling adventure , which will no doubt come in handy once the movie eventually gets released.
This is the latest exciting news for book readers after Prime Video’s Fourth Wing series found its Xaden and Violet in actors Emilio Sakraya and Esther McGregor.

articles.headline: Open-weight models win hearts, minds, and wallets
keyFacts: Open-weight models quadrupled their share of spending through Vercel's AI Gateway between June and September, processing over seven in ten tokens.
US models from Anthropic and OpenAI captured the largest share of spending in September, while Chinese AI providers also grew in popularity.
China proposed adding technology items including AI to its export control list, introducing uncertainty for US businesses relying on Chinese models, Chris McGuire said.
body: Open-weight models more than quadrupled their share of spending through Vercel's AI Gateway between June and September, when they processed more than seven in 10 tokens. "In August, open-weight models processed the majority of AI Gateway token volume for the first time," the biz said. "The money is now following. Open weight's share of spend has more than quadrupled over the last three months, from one in twenty gateway dollars in June to nearly one in four in September." AI Gateway, like OpenRouter, acts as an intermediary that allows customers to purchase tokens from different AI providers through a common interface. While it works with popular harnesses like Claude Code and Codex and provides access to proprietary and open-weight models, it doesn't see usage through other gateways or from customers who access AI models directly from vendors or through on-premises hosting. While gateway spending in September was about 13x higher than recorded in December 2025, the average price per token was about 47 percent lower, according to Vercel. At the same time, almost one in three teams changed their most-used AI provider in September, suggesting that market competition may be limiting vendor lock-in. The most popular model in September was TypeSafe AI's Jev. In just 14 days, it reached 35 percent of paid teams using Vercel's AI Gateway, the company said. Its popularity didn't generate much spending due to the model's architecture – usage accounted for only 1 percent of the month’s tokens and 0.15 percent of spending. US-based models from Anthropic and OpenAI still attract the largest portion of spending in September, with 11.03 percent going to Claude Opus 5.5, followed by GPT-6 Astra at 4.86 percent. But models from Chinese AI providers have become more popular. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ranked third in spending, at 4.19 percent. More than two-thirds of the September spending on Chinese models went to US providers serving those models, up from less than a tenth in December 2025, Vercel said. Moonshot AI, maker of Kimi, captured 3.6 percent of gateway tokens and 13.2 percent of spend in September; DeepSeek took 58 percent of tokens for just 6.6 percent of spend; and Z.ai, maker of GLM-5.3, took 7.2 percent of tokens and 4.5 percent of spend. So efforts to ban or limit open-weight models, something considered by the current US administration, would affect American businesses serving those models and their customers. Even if the US continues to dither on AI policy, trade barriers affecting AI models may alter market dynamics. China on Friday proposed adding 40 technology items to its export control list, 23 of them related to AI. The Associated Press notes that Moonshot’s Kimi K3 and Alibaba’s Qwen 3.8-Max are among the models that meet the parameter threshold set by Chinese authorities, though the official message did not identify affected models. "This introduces significant uncertainty for US businesses that host or rely on Chinese models," Chris McGuire, a senior fellow for China and emerging technologies at the Council on Foreign Relations, said in a social media post. "Particularly given that Chinese AI labs are moving toward licensing the use of open-source models to generate revenue, the Chinese government stating that it has the ability to curtail those licensing agreements at any time should make US businesses more hesitant to rely on those models going forward." McGuire said the US needs to adopt a comprehensive regulatory framework governing the use of US AI technology overseas and include Chinese AI models used or hosted in the United States in its domestic AI regulations.®

articles.headline: Red Safe Code in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Following Orders
keyFacts: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 features a locked red safe in the cabinet of the third campaign mission, Following Orders.
Players can unlock the red safe by entering the code 214 or by shooting at it directly.
Opening the safe yields a collectible note for achievement progress and an illegal contraband item.
body: Following Orders is the third mission of the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 ‘s campaign, and you can find a red safe. Once you find the safe, you can open it with the correct code, but the game doesn’t necessarily tell you where to find it or what the code is.
In this guide, I will help you figure out where the red safe is located and how to crack it open.

How to find the Red Safe in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Following Orders
Red Safe Code in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
How to find the Red Safe in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Following Orders

When the mission begins, you’ll find yourself interrogating a couple to find where the defector is. Instead of interrogating them, head to the room on the right. It’s the first room on the right when you enter the house.

Screenshot by Destructoid Head inside, open the cabinet, and you’ll find the Red Safe over there. When you find it for the first time, it remains locked. You can simply shoot at it, but using a code is the easier way to get it done.

The correct code is “214”. This code is the same for all scenarios, and it will open the safe. You have to use your arrow keys (assuming you’re on PC like me) to scroll and input the code.

A note. There are four notes you can find in this mission, and it’s one of them. Finding and reading 50 notes allows you to make progress towards one of the in-game achievements.
A contraband. These are illegal items that you can find in the campaign, and they’re also part of the in-game campaign.

articles.headline: Gloucester claim thrilling draw against Champions Cup holders Bordeaux
keyFacts: Gloucester played out a 36-36 draw against Champions Cup holders Bordeaux at Kingsholm Stadium.
Will Trenholm scored two tries for Gloucester, while Louis Bielle-Biarrey scored twice to secure a draw for Bordeaux.
Edinburgh suffered a 27-17 defeat against Toulon in their Challenge Cup opener as Malvyn Jaminet scored 22 points.
body: Champions Cup: Gloucester claim thrilling draw against holders Bordeaux

Will Trenholm scores a brace of tries as Gloucester fall just short of beating Champions Cup holders Bordeaux in a thrilling 36-36 draw; Edinburgh suffered a 27-17 defeat against Toulon in their Challenge Cup opener
Friday 16 October 2026 22:53, UK
Will Trenholm’s brace was not enough to help Gloucester pull off a stunning upset against Champions Cup holders Bordeaux, as they were forced to settle for a 36-36 draw after a dramatic contest.
George Skivington's team pushed the French outfit all the way during a pulsating European tie at Kingsholm Stadium.
Gloucester held a 24-17 lead at half-time before Trenholm crashed over twice, but a double by Louis Bielle-Biarrey salvaged a share of the spoils for visiting Bordeaux.

Bordeaux made a fast start, with Martin Page-Relo able to open the scoring in the fourth minute, but Arthur Clark produced an instant reply for Gloucester.
Efforts by Max Llewellyn and George Barton, either side of Sipili Falatea's try, earned the hosts a slender seven-point advantage at the break thanks to three successful conversions by Barton.

Pablo Uberti levelled for Bordeaux six minutes into the second period before quick-fire tries by Trenholm had Kingsholm rocking, but Bielle-Biarry levelled in the 62nd minute and despite plenty of territory, neither side could find a winning score.
Edinburgh beaten by Toulon in Challenge Cup opener
Edinburgh suffered a 27-17 defeat against Toulon in their Challenge Cup opener as Malvyn Jaminet scored 22 points for the French visitors.
Defences were on top in the first half at the Hive Stadium, with two Jaminet penalties to one from James Grayson giving Toulon a 6-3 lead at the break.

Scotland hooker Ewan Ashman hit back immediately for Edinburgh, with Grayson adding the conversion, but Fiji international Seta Tuicuvu soon barged over and Jaminet again added the extras.
Edinburgh refused to go away, with replacement Geordie Gwynn scoring with his first touch before Grayson converted to keep the hosts in contention.

But Toulon had the final say. Baptiste Serin set up Jaminet for another converted try, while Piers O'Conor's yellow card for direct contact with Jeremy Sinzelle's head compounded Edinburgh's misery and sealed their fate.

articles.headline: How to lose a job in five days
keyFacts: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia was fired on Friday after serving only five days in her position.
Her dismissal makes her the shortest-tenured White House press secretary in history.
NBC's Garrett Haake stated that the firing demonstrates a White House struggling with messaging weeks before the midterm elections.
body: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia speaks during a news briefing at the White House on October 13, 2026. | Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia is out of a job after only five days.

What happened? Zacharia was fired on Friday after less than a week in her new role, after a rocky start that included a halting performance in the briefing room, a scandal over her legal credentials, and a round of less-than-successful cleanup interviews .

The firing makes her the shortest-tenured White House press secretary in history, outstripping even first-term Trump communications director Anthony Scaramucci, who made it 10 or 11 days (figures vary) before getting the boot.

“Records are made to be broken,” Scaramucci posted on Friday . “But I take no pleasure in other people’s pain.” (No word yet on whether the “Zacharia” will emerge as a unit of time, as the “Scaramucci” has.)

What’s the context? Zacharia’s remarkably short stint behind the podium unfolded as the White House is engaged in an unprecedented attack on press freedom: The administration is still trying to ban three media outlets — CNN, MS NOW, and Politico — from the White House, though as of earlier this week, a judge is still blocking the ban from taking effect.
The diminished nature of the press secretary job was on full display in Zacharia’s sole briefing on Tuesday , when she took questions from just three outlets: Breitbart, Fox News, and the Daily Mail.

Why does this matter? Zacharia’s no good, very bad week is not likely to leave much of a lasting mark in its own right — other than, perhaps, as pub trivia — but as NBC’s Garrett Haake points out , it’s a very tangible manifestation of a White House that seems to have no idea how to spin itself out of crisis with just weeks until the midterm elections.
Most recently, Trump has landed on flat-out lying about the state of the economy — but like Zacharia’s time as press secretary, it doesn’t seem like it’s going to go all that well .
And with that, it’s time to log off…
The underlying trend — municipal inaction — may be infuriating, but I loved this story about “tactical urbanism” from my colleague Sara Herschander.

As she writes, vigilante activists have taken to painting their own crosswalks, building benches, and even installing makeshift bike lanes in their neighborhoods — and every time they do, “they remind us that it is not actually that hard — or even that expensive — to do many of the simple things that can make our cities safer and more pleasant places to live.”
You can read Sara’s full piece here , no gift link needed. Enjoy, have a great weekend, and we’ll see you on Monday!

articles.headline: Solly March set for surprise EFL transfer two months after Premier League plea
keyFacts: Reports state former Brighton winger Solly March is set to join Championship club Charlton Athletic as a free agent.
March previously stated in August that he believed he was still capable of playing in the Premier League.
Charlton manager Nathan Jones previously worked with March as an assistant and caretaker manager at Brighton.
body: Solly March is reportedly set to sign for Charlton Athletic following his summer exit from Brighton.
The winger made 300 appearances and scored 26 goals across a 13-year spell at the Seagulls.
March is heading back to the Championship with Charlton months after ending his 13-year stint with Brighton Getty
March was part of the side that finished as runners-up in the 2016/17 Championship to earn promotion to the Premier League .
Knee injuries blighted the latter years of his time on the south coast, and he has remained a free agent since the window shut.
However, as per various reports, the 32-year-old is heading back to the Championship by signing for Charlton .
The Addicks are 13th in the standings and managed by the animated Nathan Jones , who worked with the player at Brighton.
Jones was assistant to Oscar Garcia and oversaw March’s senior debut for the club.
When Sami Hyypia resigned as manager in December 2014, the now-Charlton boss played March on two occasions as Brighton caretaker.
What did March say on his future after Brighton exit?
Throughout his spell at Brighton, March played on both wings and in midfield, and even had a brief spell at left-back.
His versatility played a key role in the club becoming an established Premier League side that now competes in Europe.
However, whilst he has plenty of Championship experience thanks to his 75 appearances in the division, he was keen to stay at the top.
March told talkSPORT towards the end of the summer window that he is still capable of playing in the Premier League Getty
“For me personally, I still want to play in the Premier League,” he told talkSPORT in August, whilst also dismissing a move abroad.
“I definitely think I can do that. Maybe I’ve got to be patient, I don’t know. But it’s difficult, you get itchy feet, you’re at home alone and training alone.”
March added: “I can play many positions.
“I think I’ve got quality that maybe a lot of Premier League teams don’t have, and I think the experience helps.
“When you’ve played 300 games, you know what it’s like, and you can help the younger players and advise them.
“I still think I’ve got the quality… I’m feeling good, the best I have in two years. Just waiting for the right chance, and I think patience is the key.”
