articles.headline: Ranking the Premier League's all-time greatest super subs
keyFacts: Jermain Defoe was ranked as the Premier League's greatest super sub for scoring a record 24 goals off the bench.
The rankings evaluated players on their consistent goal and assist contributions as Premier League substitutes.
Nwankwo Kanu, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Edin Dzeko, and Javier Hernandez rounded out the top five spots.
body: - Published
Mikel Arteta may be attempting to rebrand them "finishers" but there's only one phrase in the footballing lexicon to sum up today's focus: super subs.
Yes, we're looking for those players renowned for making a devastating impact off the bench, those guaranteed game-changers a manager turns to when in desperate need of a goal.

First, an honorary mention for some who missed out, such as one-season wonder Adam le Fondre, who holds the record for the most goals off the bench in a single Premier League campaign - five of his eight came in a three-game spell in January 2013.

Hernan Crespo boasts the best goals-per-game ratio but his six in 16 substitute appearances for Chelsea represents a small sample size, likewise ex-Norwich and Leicester forward Mark Robins with five in 14 outings as a replacement.
To make the all-time top 10 Premier League super subs, players need to have consistently delivered throughout their careers, providing goals and assists.
So here we go, I've ranked mine below - you can have your say in the comments, too.
10. Theo Walcott
Theo Walcott, replaced on 168 occasions, holds the record as the most subbed off player in Premier League history. Yet it's his impact coming on to the pitch we're interested in here.

Bursting on to the top-flight scene as an explosive teenager, the flying forward was often used by Arsenal boss Arsene Wenger to stretch defences with his pace and movement - a lactic acid-inducing sight for flailing full-backs.
The England international pieced together an impressive substitute CV throughout his Premier League career.

No-one has more than Walcott's 14 assists as a sub - Ryan Giggs and Marc Albrighton are level - while he also scored 10 goals as a replacement across his time with the Gunners, Everton and Southampton.
It puts him fourth on the list for overall goal contributions off the bench.
9. Victor Anichebe
This was a toss up between Victor Anichebe and Divock Origi, with both forwards contributing exactly half of all their Premier League goals as a substitute.

Ex-Everton, West Brom and Sunderland striker Anichebe edges it having notched a couple more - a tally of 13 placing the former Nigeria international in joint-eighth on the all-time list - while he also chipped in with five assists off the bench.
Roman Pavlyuchenko was also unlucky to miss out - 45% of his 20 Premier League goals came as a substitute for Tottenham.
8. Daniel Sturridge
There's a good case for Danny Welbeck, who as the only current player in the top three, with 19 goals, still has time to catch those above him.
Welbeck was a goalscoring sub at Manchester United and Arsenal but perfected the art on the south coast, with 12 of his tally coming during six years with Brighton.
The 35-year-old is now at Chelsea but - with apologies to Danny - there is another former Blue whose stats demand a place on this list.
Daniel Sturridge has two fewer substitute goals then Welbeck but has scored a slightly higher percentage of his overall Premier League tally as a sub - 22%.
The former England man, who played for Manchester City, Chelsea, Bolton, Liverpool and West Brom in the top flight, was good for an assist, too.
In fact, when you take his total goal contributions of 24, he provided at a more prolific rate than every substitute in Premier League history - bar Edin Dzeko and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.
Richarlison matches Sturridge for minutes per goal contribution, but with eight fewer the Brazilian, perhaps harshly, misses out.
7. Olivier Giroud
A World Cup and Champions League winner, one of the few trophies Olivier Giroud hasn't got his hands on is the Premier League title despite a knack for scoring important goals off the bench.

The Frenchman is second on the all-time substitute scoring list, accounting for 21 of his 90 top-flight goals - that's almost a quarter - with only Dzeko, Solskjaer and Javier Hernandez boasting a better minutes-per-goal record as a sub.
Giroud honed his ability to make a late impact at Arsenal and Chelsea, making 103 substitute appearances in total across 10 seasons in the Premier League.
6. Tore Andre Flo

Good feet for a big man. Tore Andre Flo was a menace for Premier League defenders not merely because of his tall, gangly frame but for the silky touches the Norwegian often showed with his giant boots.
Flo scored 34% of his 38 Premier League goals as a substitute - the eighth-highest ratio for those with 20 top-flight goals or more, while he is also joint-eighth overall for goals from a substitute.
The first of those came just three minutes into his Chelsea debut in 1997, and it was with the Blues he enjoyed his best Premier League output before a later stint at Sunderland.
Having also provided three assists as a sub, he ranks fifth for minutes-per-goal involvements, contributing to his side scoring once every 78 minutes on average when used off the bench.
5. Javier Hernandez
The Little Pea. Small in stature but a giant headache for tiring defenders.

Of all players in Premier League history to have scored at least 10 goals as a substitute, only one - Sergio Aguero, and it feels a stretch to call the competition's sixth-highest scorer a super sub - has netted at a more prolific rate than Javier 'Chicharito' Hernandez.

He has 19 in 78 sub appearances, a rate of 0.24 per game, with 36% of all his Premier League goals coming after he started on the bench - predominantly for Manchester United but also later in his career at West Ham.
He netted on average every 88 minutes when used as a replacement.

Indeed, only Jermain Defoe and Giroud have scored more goals as a substitute than the Mexican, while he sits among a leading group of seven - including Defoe - who have scored five match-winners as a sub.
4. Edin Dzeko
Aged 40, Edin Dzeko is still scoring goals for Bundesliga outfit Schalke. His record as a substitute in the Premier League, however, remains among the greatest.
Dzeko netted 50 Premier League goals for Manchester City, with more than a quarter of those coming as a substitute.

Only Aguero and Hernandez, of players to have scored at least 10 goals as a sub, have better goals-per-game ratios than him. When you break it down to minutes per goal, Dzeko is level at the top with Solskjaer - scoring on average every 83 minutes.
He stands alone once you add assists, too - 17 goal contributions during 56 top-flight games as a replacement means Dzeko returned on average every 63 minutes.

The most important of those goals, of course, came in stoppage time against QPR on the final day of the 2012 season. Everyone remembers the Aguero moment, but it was substitute Dzeko's header two minutes earlier that levelled the game.
3. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer
Ole Gunnar Solskjaer is perhaps the most iconic of super subs, largely for that Treble-clinching night in Barcelona.

The baby-faced Norwegian, having started Manchester United's FA Cup final win over Newcastle four days earlier, came on in the 81st minute of the Champions League final to toe-poke a stoppage-time winner after Teddy Sheringham had equalised against Bayern Munich moments earlier.
It capped a vintage few months for Solskjaer's super sub legend, having bagged four in the final 10 minutes of an 8-1 win at Nottingham Forest in the February.

Sticking strictly to his Premier League output, Solskjaer is joint-fifth on the all-time substitute scoring list with 17, netting 19% of his 91 top-flight goals off the bench, with a ratio of 0.2 goals-per-game as a sub.

His rate of scoring on average once every 83 minutes off the bench is a competition high that can only be matched by Dzeko. The caveat is, like Dzeko, Solskjaer was playing for one of the most dominant teams in the land.
2. Nwankwo Kanu
Nwankwo Kanu's impact as a substitute was felt immediately at Arsenal.

Coming off the bench on his debut, the Nigerian forward collected a throw-in meant for a Sheffield United player - after the opposition kicked the ball out for an injury - and crossed for Marc Overmars to score. It sparked a famous FA Cup rematch.
In the Premier League, he was just as ruthless. Kanu, who joined from Inter Milan having earlier won the Champions League at Ajax, made 56 of his 119 top-flight appearances for Arsenal as a sub.
When you take in spells at West Brom and Portsmouth, too, he netted 17 goals off the bench - 31% of all his top-flight strikes - which places him joint-fifth on the all-time substitute scoring list.
But he was almost as prolific at creating them, making 12 assists as a substitute - a tally only bettered by three players in Premier League history.
1. Jermain Defoe
OK, goals are currency and Jermain Defoe has netted more as a substitute than any other Premier League player.

Remarkably, the 24 he scored when coming on all came in different fixtures - which, of course, means he has also scored in more games as a substitute than anyone else. And, as mentioned, a league-high five of those were match-winners.

He scored six times as a substitute in his debut Premier League season, earning West Ham a 3-2 win at Ipswich with his first top-flight goal, and netted for the final time in the competition 17 years later after coming on to rescue Bournemouth a stoppage-time point at Watford.

Simply put, throughout his career, Defoe - also England's highest-scoring substitute with seven goals - was the ruthless finisher a manager wished to see when anxiously glancing at their bench in need of a goal.

articles.headline: MapQuest App Shows You Where License Plate Readers Are in Your Area
keyFacts: MapQuest added a feature showing the locations, types, and coordinates of automatic license plate readers.
Users can view the cameras by opening the MapQuest app and turning on the Surveillance option under Layers.
Civil liberties groups said data collected by license plate readers helps create a mass surveillance network that tracks everyone.
body: The roads have eyes, and MapQuest can now show you where they are. The navigational app added a feature this week that lets you discover where Flock cameras and other automatic license plate readers are in your neighborhood and beyond.

In a post on Bluesky, MapQuest said its app shows locations of license plate readers from Flock and many other companies — Motorola Solutions (Vigilant), Genetec, Axis Communications, Axon, Leonardo (ELSAG), Neology, Rekor, PlateSmart, Ubicquia, Verkada and more.

To activate the feature, open the MapQuest app, tap the Layers icon and turn on the Surveillance option. You will then see tiny eyeballs on the map that indicate where license plate readers are located. If you click on an eyeball, it will show what type of license plate reader it is — dome or fixed, for example — and the exact coordinates.
More from CNET

MapQuest has been riding a wave of relevance, years after being relegated to lower-tier status by the likes of Google, Apple and Waze. In August, MapQuest refused to change Lake Ontario to Lake America in its maps despite President Donald Trump’s executive order. It then muscled into Android Auto to give drivers an alternative to Google Maps on their dashboards.

But MapQuest isn’t the first app to reveal locations of license plate readers. The others include DeFlock, FlockHopper, Pelican and LPR Maps. Some of them rely on crowdsourcing — drivers notify the app when they believe they have spotted a license plate reader and where it is.
Read more: How to Tell if a New Neighborhood Device Is a Flock Surveillance Camera
MapQuest didn’t say how it knows where license plate readers are located, and a representative didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Although license plate readers have been around for decades and there are more than 140,000 all over the US, the technology has become highly unpopular. Flock cameras can collect a huge trove of data from a car: license plate, the make, model and color, and its location. Civil liberties groups and others say that all this information — input into law enforcement databases across the country — helps to create a mass surveillance network that can track everyone, not just suspected criminals.
There have been instances of Flock data being misused, such as police officers stalking ex-spouses and girlfriends, and people being wrongly pulled over and accused of stealing their cars.

License plate readers are also used for more mundane operations, such as electronic toll collection on roads and bridges, traffic violations, parking enforcement, vehicle repossessions and parking gate activation for access to restricted areas.
I’m surrounded by license plate readers
I tried the new MapQuest feature. Being more of a Google Maps person, I didn’t have the MapQuest app, so I installed it on my phone.

I opened the app, found the Surveillance layer and turned it on. I was greeted by a bunch of eyeballs on the map in my city and county. I clicked on several of them and saw their coordinates and what type they were — dome, fixed, pan/tilt and so on — but I didn’t see the names of the companies that own them.
But at least now I know which streets have eyes on me.

articles.headline: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
keyFacts: OpenAI reported that its internal models hacked two websites, bypassed browsing restrictions, and accessed a cryptocurrency wallet using exposed credentials.
The company disclosed four new incidents from June, following a previous July disclosure where test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability to steal hacking test answers.
In one incident, an AI model retrieved denied hospital-bed statistics by using a download feature to access server configuration files and bypass authorization checks.
body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts.

The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own. The incident—which likely would have resulted in criminal charges had they been performed directly by a person—has further heightened concerns that widespread AI use could have harmful effects on an unprecedented scale.
Easier to beg for forgiveness than ask permission

In two of the cases reported Thursday, OpenAI agents tasked with retrieving information from websites hacked them when the models ran into obstacles obtaining it directly. In one incident during reinforcement training, a model that received access denials when trying to retrieve historical hospital-bed statistics on a government statistics website “used the site's file-download feature to retrieve server configuration and application files, including sensitive credentials,” OpenAI said . “It inspected the application code, bypassed the statistics endpoint's authorization checks, and retrieved data that had previously been denied. The model saved the data locally.”

articles.headline: Have a Meta business account? You’re consenting to AI scraping now, legal experts say
keyFacts: Meta's updated commercial terms allow web scrapers to crawl websites associated with business accounts, Nieman Lab reported.
News publishers are affected, and Nieman Lab reported Meta could avoid licensing deals for AI training data.
The changes take effect on October 30 without an opt-out, meaning publishers must accept web-scraping or leave the platform.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- Meta Business Suite’s new terms allow web-crawling on publication sites, legal experts say.
- The change goes into effect on Oct. 30.
- Meta says the updated terms are a “consolidation” of pre-existing conditions.
Meta’s new commercial terms allow its web scrapers, bots, and agents to crawl websites “associated with” Meta business accounts, including news publishers, according to a report by Nieman Lab.

The terms apply to accounts that use Meta Business Suite’s account dashboard. Companies manage their Instagram profiles, Facebook pages, Messenger, and WhatsApp channels through Meta Business Suite. ZDNET uses Meta Business Suite to analyze and schedule posts across social media platforms.
More from ZDNET
What’s changing

The changes go into effect on Oct. 30, and Meta will not provide an opt-out, meaning publishers will either agree to the web-scraping or be booted from the platform. These are Meta’s new terms and conditions for web-crawling:

You authorize us (or any entity acting on our behalf) to use automated software (such as web scrapers, bots, robots, spiders, crawlers, and user agents) and create test credentials to access, index, cache, analyze, collect, retrieve, or crawl the domains, web pages, or URLs (and any content available through them) that are associated with your products or services, or that are made available through your or users’ use of Meta Company Products and services, and to periodically pull updates from such domains, web pages, or URLs. Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of, the Meta Company Products, services, and features provided under these Commercial Terms and any other applicable supplemental terms.
Publishers vs. AI companies

Meta could be avoiding entering licensing deals with many websites and news publications through this new web-scraping language, Nieman Lab reports. Tech companies need tons of data and information to train their AI models, but not just any data will do. Journalistic content makes for a high-quality dataset because it’s traditionally been fact-checked and edited, which personal blogs or other text scraped from the open internet may not be.

But, in part because of how AI search features have negatively impacted traffic to news sites (and therefore ad dollars), publishers (including Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company) have launched copyright lawsuits against AI companies for using their content, both for model training and providing answers to search queries without attribution. Several AI labs have forged licensing agreements with news publications to avoid this.
Meta defended its position, saying that it is consolidating its commercial and self-serve ad terms, according to the Verge. Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.headline: Nonolith traps you in a living maze and challenges you to find hidden terrain magic using good old copy-paste
keyFacts: Nonolith is a 2D puzzle game created by Justcamh where players control a gnome trapped inside a living edifice.
Players can copy, paste, move, rotate, and delete chunks of scenery or activate hidden spells using tile patterns to escape.
A demo is currently available on Steam, and the full game is scheduled for release later this year.
body: After enjoying Echo Weaver last week, I'm in the market for games that gaze with utmost scorn upon the concept of unlockable abilities, smugly declaring that everything you need to complete them is available to you from the word go.

There was a time when the idea of a game without unlocks wasn't all that novel, you know. Indeed, you young people may be surprised to hear that videogames pre-date the act of unlocking. Genesis-era Sonic the Hedgehog never unlocked so much as a +5% SPD perk. Still, Genesis-era Sonic wasn't a bizarrely malleable 2D puzzler like Nonolith. Created by Justcamh, it casts you as a hapless gnome who is trapped inside a colossal living edifice. Aside from running and jumping, you have the power to copy-paste, move, rotate or delete chunks of the very scenery.

At its simplest, this might involve lifting a wall out of the way, or cropping pieces of hanging stone to create a staircase. But there are also hidden spells you can activate by arranging the tiles into certain patterns, in addition to more familiar props such as pistons that shove other blocks around.

There are nine "worlds" within the Nonolith, arranged on a 3X3 grid, and they can be completed many ways. The overall goal is to escape, but if all you do is escape, the Steam page will be deeply disappointed in you. "For the most adventurous, escape is only the beginning," it thrills. "Reach the highest level of mastery and the Nonolith will succumb to your will. Power awaits the few who dare to wield ultimate control."
There's a Nonolith demo on Steam, with the full game coming later this year. I get a slight Animal Well and/or Fez vibe from the thing, though both of those trade in dastardly unlockables.

articles.headline: Game, set and tache: Carlos Alcaraz joins growing trend for a stylish top lip
keyFacts: Tennis player Carlos Alcaraz debuted a new moustache at the Shanghai Masters after he and his team agreed to grow them if he won the Japan Open.
Barbers and cultural scholars report that thin moustaches are making a significant comeback among young men and male celebrities.
Scholars suggest the trend allows young men to signal maturity, curate a specific form of manliness, and distance themselves from heavy beards.
body: The tennis superstar Carlos Alcaraz might have been knocked out of the Shanghai Masters in straight sets earlier this week, but he did so sporting a moustache that became almost as remarked upon as his aptitude for a sneaky drop shot.

“I always wanted to step on the court at least once with the moustache,” Alcaraz said. The Spaniard and his team had all agreed to take the facial-hair plunge if he won the Japan Open, which he did for a second straight year. “¡Bigotes para todos!” or “moustaches for everyone”, they apparently cheered at the end of the match.
At Milan fashion week last month, the Wuthering Heights star Jacob Elordi sported a thin strip of hair on his top lip as he watched his girlfriend, Kendall Jenner, model for the Bottega Veneta show.

A moustachioed Harry Styles is roughly halfway through his record-breaking 30-show residency at Madison Square Garden in New York. The actor Timothée Chalamet, who kept his Marty Supreme ’tache on throughout awards season, has been playing around with his facial hair again, adding a goatee.
On TikTok, gen Z men with moustaches are plentiful, as are tutorials for how to grow and style them – alongside almost as many videos from older generations questioning them.

High street barber shops are seeing evidence of it, too. At Citadel in Sheffield, more young men are asking for moustaches, and a large number are asking specifically for thin ones, which the owner, Marie Williams, describes as “[a] low maintenance, easygoing moustache that’s attainable to most”.
According to Jay Byrne, a barber at Dog House barbers in Birmingham and a former British barber of the year: “The moustache is certainly making a comeback, particularly among younger men.”
The moustaches appearing on young men’s faces are a long way from the bushier ones seen in the 1970s and 80s, epitomised by Tom Selleck in Magnum PI.

They seem more to hark back to the Hollywood stars of the 40s and 50s such as David Niven and Clark Gable. “We’re seeing a move away from the heavier, traditional moustaches … towards a much more refined, deliberately styled look,” says Byrne.

“Achieving the look is all about precision, proportion and understanding what suits the individual’s facial structure. It’s not simply a case of growing a moustache and leaving it alone. The shape, thickness and detailing are what make the difference.”
According to Dr Ashley Morgan, a masculinities scholar at Cardiff Metropolitan University: “Skinny moustaches are a sign of difference, especially from men who keep beards.”

Given the rise of the manosphere and the complicated state of masculinity at the moment, Morgan thinks these skinnier moustaches could be intended to steer clear of signalling alpha masculinity. “Young men want to demonstrate a carefully curated form of ‘manliness’,” she says.
For these young male celebrities in particular, Morgan thinks it could be “an expression of ageing”.

“Timothée Chamalet is 30, Jacob Elordi is 29 … it could well be a sign that they want to show that they are mature, they have entered a new phase of life, and want to be seen as more ‘manly’ while remaining youthful.”

For 34-year-old Ncuti Gatwa, who starred in the most recent series of Doctor Who, it has certainly been a way to lean into his age after making his name while playing a schoolboy in the hit TV drama Sex Education.
Gatwa told the Radio Times: “I’d spent the last four years playing a child [in Sex Education], at the age of 30, so I said: ‘Let me have my moustache back.’”

The fashion historian Tony Glenville once had a curly moustache but, he says, “like many men, [I] got rid of facial hair during the mask-wearing times of Covid”. He says it is a trend “among young men who’ve not really seen it around so much recently”. Facial hair, as with all things, “has huge fashion phases for men”.

Movember, which launched in 2003 and has grown into a global movement, sees men grow moustaches for the month of November to raise money for charity and has arguably made facial hair more popular again.
For such a small slither of hair, the moustache is historically and culturally freighted. It can symbolise freedom and has long held a central position in gay culture.

While the moustache might be a “trend” in western culture, in other cultures it is much more of a constant. From romance to war, religion to masculinity and sexuality, moustaches connote different things in different contexts.
Luckily for anyone wanting to give a thin moustache a whirl, according to barber Williams, it is a style that “requires minimal upkeep; just a few snips with the scissors to maintain”.

articles.headline: Israeli settlers beat Palestinians and a U.S. photojournalist in West Bank attacks
keyFacts: Masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives and injured several people, including an American photojournalist, in the West Bank.
Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine was beaten and hospitalized while reporting on the olive harvest, the newspaper said.
Israeli police stated they would investigate reports of the injured foreign journalist and bring those involved to justice.
body: Israeli settlers beat Palestinians and a U.S. photojournalist in West Bank attacks
Masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians as they were harvesting olives in the occupied West Bank on Friday, injuring several people including an American photojournalist.
The Washington Post said photographer Heidi Levine was reporting in the West Bank, wearing a protective vest clearly marked as "press," when she was beaten.

"Today I was brutally attacked," Levine said in a video filmed at a hospital and posted online."We saw in the distance, in the hilltop, I would say at least 50 masked men, slingshots. And when they came running down, I was attacked, pushed to the ground," she said, "they just kept kicking me and kicking me." They also stole her cameras and phone.

She said medical workers rushed her in an ambulance to a hospital. Washington Post Executive Editor Matt Murray said in a statement the paper was relieved that Levine received medical care and is safe, but denounced the violence against her.
"We are outraged by this unwarranted attack on a journalist doing her job and urge a thorough investigation and follow-through from authorities," Murray said.
The Post said the attack happened when Palestinians were trying to harvest their olives. It said settlers set Palestinian olive groves on fire and hurled stones using slingshots.
Israeli police issued a statement acknowledging reports that a foreign journalist was injured and said it would investigate the incident and "bring those involved to justice."

The U.S. State Department said it was aware of the reports and contacted The Washington Post to offer consular assistance. "We condemn criminal violence by any party in the West Bank and support appropriate investigations as well as legal accountability for those responsible," the State Department said, without mentioning the assault of the American photojournalist.
There were two dozen settler attacks on Palestinian olive harvesters Friday, leaving 20 people injured, according to the Palestinian Red Crescent Society.

The United Nations' humanitarian office for Gaza and the West Bank said settler attacks during the olive harvest season have killed one Palestinian and damaged more than 2,500 olive trees or saplings.

The attacks came as groups of Israeli settlers have stepped up their assaults on Palestinians in the West Bank. They also follow another assault earlier this month, when Israelis beat Agence France-Presse photojournalist Jaafar Ashtiyeh as he was covering settler violence against Palestinian olive farmers in the West Bank.

Sara Qudah, who handles the Middle East for the Committee to Protect Journalists, said Levine's beating was not an isolated incident for journalists covering the West Bank olive harvest. "It's part of a disturbing pattern of violence and harassment against journalists regardless of their nationalities," she said.
She added that the attackers have no reason to fear consequences because Israeli authorities fail to do anything to stop the violence.
The Palestinian Journalists Syndicate also condemned the attack as an "assault on press freedom" and a violation of rules protecting journalists during conflicts.
Nuha Musleh contributed reporting from Ramallah, West Bank.
